Master the two essential conditions of polygon similarity, vertex correspondence order, similarity ratio (k), special quadrilateral criteria, perimeter ratio theorem, and algebraic unknown solutions (x,y,zx, y, zx,y,z).

Prerequisites & Diagnostic Review

Review foundational concepts required before studying polygon similarity: ratios, sum of quadrilateral angles, and quadrilateral properties.

Prerequisite Review

Ratio & Proportionality

A ratio compares two quantities ab\frac{a}{b}ba​. Two ratios are equal ab=cd=k\frac{a}{b} = \frac{c}{d} = kba​=dc​=k if they simplify to the same constant factor kkk. Cross-multiplication yields a×d=b×ca \times d = b \times ca×d=b×c.

Quadrilateral Angle Sum

The sum of the measures of the interior angles of any convex quadrilateral is always 360∘360^\circ360∘. If 3 angles are known, the 4th is: m(∠4)=360∘−(∠1+∠2+∠3)m(\angle 4) = 360^\circ - (\angle_1 + \angle_2 + \angle_3)m(∠4)=360∘−(∠1​+∠2​+∠3​).

Special Quadrilateral Properties

In a parallelogram/rhombus: opposite angles are equal (m(∠A)=m(∠C)m(\angle A) = m(\angle C)m(∠A)=m(∠C)), and consecutive angles are supplementary (m(∠A)+m(∠B)=180∘m(\angle A) + m(\angle B) = 180^\circm(∠A)+m(∠B)=180∘). In rectangles and squares, all 4 angles are 90∘90^\circ90∘.

Precision Plots & Modeling
Egyptian Heritage & Archaeological Modeling • Statue of King Thutmose III
STEM Real-World Application

The ancient Egyptians carved monumental statues for grand temples. Modern museum curators and 3D preservation labs rely on geometric similarity to produce exact miniature replicas with authentic proportions.

Mathematical Connection & STEM Analysis:
Mathematical Proportional Modeling:
Because the miniature replica is geometrically similar to the original statue (height 195 cm195\text{ cm}195 cm, width 58 cm58\text{ cm}58 cm), corresponding linear dimensions are directly proportional: Height of ReplicaHeight of Original=Width of ReplicaWidth of Original  ⟹  h195=558\frac{\text{Height of Replica}}{\text{Height of Original}} = \frac{\text{Width of Replica}}{\text{Width of Original}} \implies \frac{h}{195} = \frac{5}{58}Height of OriginalHeight of Replica​=Width of OriginalWidth of Replica​⟹195h​=585​ Applying cross-multiplication yields 58h=975  ⟹  h=97558≈16.81 cm58h = 975 \implies h = \frac{975}{58} \approx 16.81\text{ cm}58h=975⟹h=58975​≈16.81 cm. This uniform scale factor preserves the authentic pharaonic proportions with zero distortion.
Digital Media & Optics • Cinema Screen vs TV Aspect Ratios
STEM Real-World Application

Modern entertainment screens rely strictly on geometric similarity (aspect ratios) to display high-definition films without image distortion or black letterbox cropping.

Mathematical Connection & STEM Analysis:
Geometric Aspect Ratio Proof:
A cinema screen measuring 45 ft×25 ft45\text{ ft} \times 25\text{ ft}45 ft×25 ft has an aspect ratio of 4525=95=1.80\frac{45}{25} = \frac{9}{5} = 1.802545​=59​=1.80. A TV screen measuring 36 in×20 in36\text{ in} \times 20\text{ in}36 in×20 in possesses the identical ratio 3620=1.80\frac{36}{20} = 1.802036​=1.80, making it geometrically similar to the cinema screen. Consequently, TV 2 displays the cinema film with complete fidelity, while older 4:34:34:3 monitors (frac3627≈1.33\\frac{36}{27} \approx 1.33frac3627≈1.33) force image compression or letterbox bars.

Essential Curriculum Standards Definitions & Standard Forms
1

Two Simultaneous Conditions

Equality of angles alone is NOT sufficient (e.g. rectangle vs square), nor is proportionality of sides alone sufficient (e.g. rhombus vs square). Both must hold true!

2

Vertex Correspondence Order

Vertices must be written in exact corresponding order: ABCD∼EFGH  ⟹  A↔E,B↔F,C↔G,D↔HABCD \sim EFGH \implies A \leftrightarrow E, B \leftrightarrow F, C \leftrightarrow G, D \leftrightarrow HABCD∼EFGH⟹A↔E,B↔F,C↔G,D↔H. Side ratios follow immediately: ABEF=BCFG=…\frac{AB}{EF} = \frac{BC}{FG} = \dotsEFAB​=FGBC​=…

3

Similarity Ratio / Scale Factor kkk

If k>1k > 1k>1, polygon 1 is an Enlargement of polygon 2. If 0<k<10 < k < 10<k<1, it is a Reduction. If k=1k = 1k=1, the polygons are Congruent.

4

Transitivity Principle

Two polygons similar to a third polygon are similar to each other. In addition, all congruent polygons are similar (k=1k = 1k=1), but similar polygons are NOT necessarily congruent.

🏛️ Special Quadrilateral Criteria & Regular Polygons

Geometric Analysis

1. All Squares Are Similar

  • • All 4 angles are right angles (90∘=90∘90^\circ = 90^\circ90∘=90∘).
  • • All 4 sides are equal, so side ratios are always constant: ab=ab=⋯=k\frac{a}{b} = \frac{a}{b} = \dots = kba​=ba​=⋯=k.

2. Rhombuses: One Angle Suffices

  • • Two rhombuses are similar if one pair of corresponding angles is equal (m(∠A)=m(∠E)m(\angle A) = m(\angle E)m(∠A)=m(∠E)).
  • • Because all 4 sides of each rhombus are equal, side proportionality is guaranteed automatically!

3. Rectangles: Proportional Dimensions

  • • All interior angles are 90∘90^\circ90∘ automatically.
  • • Two rectangles are similar if and only if their two adjacent dimensions are proportional: Length1Length2=Width1Width2\frac{\text{Length}_1}{\text{Length}_2} = \frac{\text{Width}_1}{\text{Width}_2}Length2​Length1​​=Width2​Width1​​.

4. Regular Polygons: Same Side Count

  • • Regular polygons having the same number of sides are always similar (e.g. all equilateral triangles, all regular hexagons).
  • • Spot the Error: Regular polygons with different numbers of sides (e.g. regular triangle and regular pentagon) are NEVER similar!

Idea 3: Special Quadrilateral Similarity Criteria

Mastery Strategy: Remember the quick tests: (1) All squares are always similar. (2) Rectangles only need L1L2=W1W2\frac{L_1}{L_2} = \frac{W_1}{W_2}L2​L1​​=W2​W1​​. (3) Rhombuses only need one angle equal (m(∠1)=m(∠2)m(\angle 1) = m(\angle 2)m(∠1)=m(∠2)). (4) Parallelograms need one angle equal AND adjacent sides proportional! Every question is presented on its own dedicated canvas.

Solved Example 3.1 • Rectangles Only (Textbook Page 50)
Problem: Prove that Rectangle ABCDABCDABCD (length BC=6 cmBC = 6\text{ cm}BC=6 cm, width CD=4 cmCD = 4\text{ cm}CD=4 cm) is similar to Rectangle XYZMXYZMXYZM (length YZ=3 cmYZ = 3\text{ cm}YZ=3 cm, width ZM=2 cmZM = 2\text{ cm}ZM=2 cm), and calculate the similarity ratio of ABCDABCDABCD to XYZMXYZMXYZM.
Step 1: Verify Angles
In any rectangle, all four interior angles are right angles (90∘90^\circ90∘). Therefore, all corresponding angles are automatically equal.
Step 2: Compare Dimension Ratios
Evaluate the ratio between corresponding lengths and widths:
BCYZ=63=2,CDZM=42=2\frac{BC}{YZ} = \frac{6}{3} = 2, \quad \frac{CD}{ZM} = \frac{4}{2} = 2YZBC​=36​=2,ZMCD​=24​=2
Step 3: Conclusion
Since corresponding dimensions are proportional (BCYZ=CDZM=2\frac{BC}{YZ} = \frac{CD}{ZM} = 2YZBC​=ZMCD​=2), the two rectangles are similar.
Rectangle ABCD∼ABCD \simABCD∼ Rectangle XYZMXYZMXYZM, and the similarity ratio is k=2k = 2k=2.
Solved Example 3.2 • Rhombuses Only (Textbook Page 50)
Problem: Prove that Rhombus ABCDABCDABCD (side length AB=3 cmAB = 3\text{ cm}AB=3 cm, angle m(∠D)=110∘m(\angle D) = 110^\circm(∠D)=110∘) is similar to Rhombus EFGHEFGHEFGH (side length EF=5 cmEF = 5\text{ cm}EF=5 cm, angle m(∠G)=70∘m(\angle G) = 70^\circm(∠G)=70∘), and calculate the similarity ratio of ABCDABCDABCD to EFGHEFGHEFGH.
Step 1: Calculate Supplementary Angle
In rhombus ABCDABCDABCD, consecutive angles are supplementary:
m(∠C)=180∘−110∘=70∘m(\angle C) = 180^\circ - 110^\circ = 70^\circm(∠C)=180∘−110∘=70∘
Step 2: Angle Equality
Since m(∠C)=70∘m(\angle C) = 70^\circm(∠C)=70∘ and m(∠G)=70∘m(\angle G) = 70^\circm(∠G)=70∘, one pair of corresponding angles is equal. In any rhombus, having one matching angle guarantees all four angles are equal in pairs (70∘70^\circ70∘ and 110∘110^\circ110∘).
Step 3: Side Proportionality
All four sides are equal within each rhombus. Thus, the ratio of every corresponding side is identical: ABEF=35\frac{AB}{EF} = \frac{3}{5}EFAB​=53​.
Rhombus ABCD∼ABCD \simABCD∼ Rhombus EFGHEFGHEFGH, and the similarity ratio is k=35k = \frac{3}{5}k=53​.

Idea 4: Ratio of Perimeters & Solving Algebraic Systems (x, y, z)

Perimeter Theorem: The ratio of the perimeters of two similar polygons is equal to the similarity ratio kkk of any two corresponding sides: Perimeter1Perimeter2=k\frac{\text{Perimeter}_1}{\text{Perimeter}_2} = kPerimeter2​Perimeter1​​=k. Equate each side expression to kkk to solve for algebraic variables x,y,zx, y, zx,y,z!

Perimeter Ratio Property
By the perimeter theorem: ABEF=BCFG=CDGH=Perimeter of ABCDPerimeter of EFGH=32\frac{AB}{EF} = \frac{BC}{FG} = \frac{CD}{GH} = \frac{\text{Perimeter of } ABCD}{\text{Perimeter of } EFGH} = \frac{3}{2}EFAB​=FGBC​=GHCD​=Perimeter of EFGHPerimeter of ABCD​=23​.
Solving for z
ABEF=32  ⟹  6z=32  ⟹  3z=12  ⟹  z=4\frac{AB}{EF} = \frac{3}{2} \implies \frac{6}{z} = \frac{3}{2} \implies 3z = 12 \implies z = 4EFAB​=23​⟹z6​=23​⟹3z=12⟹z=4
Solving for y
BCFG=32  ⟹  y+35=32  ⟹  2(y+3)=15  ⟹  2y+6=15  ⟹  2y=9  ⟹  y=4.5\frac{BC}{FG} = \frac{3}{2} \implies \frac{y + 3}{5} = \frac{3}{2} \implies 2(y + 3) = 15 \implies 2y + 6 = 15 \implies 2y = 9 \implies y = 4.5FGBC​=23​⟹5y+3​=23​⟹2(y+3)=15⟹2y+6=15⟹2y=9⟹y=4.5
Solving for x
CDGH=32  ⟹  2x+1x+2=32  ⟹  2(2x+1)=3(x+2)\frac{CD}{GH} = \frac{3}{2} \implies \frac{2x + 1}{x + 2} = \frac{3}{2} \implies 2(2x + 1) = 3(x + 2)GHCD​=23​⟹x+22x+1​=23​⟹2(2x+1)=3(x+2)
4x+2=3x+6  ⟹  4x−3x=6−2  ⟹  x=44x + 2 = 3x + 6 \implies 4x - 3x = 6 - 2 \implies x = 44x+2=3x+6⟹4x−3x=6−2⟹x=4
x=4x = 4x=4,    y=4.5y = 4.5y=4.5,    z=4z = 4z=4.

Question 8 of 10

Teacher asked: 'Are all regular polygons similar?' Ahmed answered: 'Yes, all regular polygons are similar.' Nourhan answered: 'No, they are only similar if they have the same number of sides.' Who is correct?

Complete Mathematical Proof:

Nourhan is correct. Regular polygons can only be similar if they have the identical number of sides. An equilateral triangle (3 sides) can never be similar to a regular hexagon (6 sides) or a square (4 sides).

Question 10 of 10

Which of the following conditions is sufficient by itself to guarantee that two rhombuses are similar?

Complete Mathematical Proof:

All rhombuses already have four equal sides. Therefore, if just one pair of corresponding angles is equal (m(∠A)=m(∠E)m(\angle A) = m(\angle E)m(∠A)=m(∠E)), all corresponding angles will be equal, making the rhombuses similar.
